Corning Chakan._comment: Pune site, one counter, seven days a week (`serve_weekends` is true, which the soup/sweet schedule below depends on). Slots: soup, bread, rice, white_rice, veg_dry, veg_gravy, dal, dessert, starter — one dish each. The starter category now EXISTS on the counter, so the Thursday chaat rules below are live; they were written while it did not and their comments said so. Five of the client's fourteen rules need no per-client entry because Pune's own ruleset already enforces them at least as tightly: 'kabuli chana gravy max once a week' is `kabuli_chana_gravy_weekly`, 'legume-based gravies max once a week' is `legume_gravy_weekly`, and 'mixed-veg, veg kurma and veg kofta max twice a week' is covered by `mixed_veg_gravy_weekly` + `veg_kurma_gravy_weekly` + `veg_kofta_gravy_weekly` (one day each) — the union cap below is added anyway because the client stated the combined number, and a city rule can be relaxed later without the client's requirement quietly going with it. 'Sweet and soup on alternate days' is not a rule: it is what the two day-restrictions below already produce (sweet Mon/Wed/Fri, soup Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun). 'Soya can be served as one of the vegetable options' is permission, not a constraint, so nothing enforces it — Pune carries soya veg dries and gravies and they are already eligible.
Corning Chakan._meal_shared_why: 'dessert, soup and indian bread shall be the same as Lunch' — the DINNER service repeats the lunch dish for these three slots, on the same day. It is the exact opposite of the planner's default, which bans every lunch dish at dinner (note 39), so it cannot be a solver rule: the two services are separate solves and neither can see the other. The planner pins the lunch dish in and leaves these slots out of the exclusion it would otherwise send. `bread` is here for completeness and is already true by another route — the chapati pin below is client-wide, so both services serve it anyway; listing it means the requirement survives the pin being changed. Soup and dessert are the halves that actually need this: both are day-restricted at this site and the dish varies by day.

rules._comment: 'Soup should be served on Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday.' The station stands down on the other three days, which is the half of the alternation that puts soup opposite the sweet.
rules.name: corning_chakan_soup_tue_thu_sat_sun

rules._comment: 'Sweets should be served on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.' The other half. Together with the soup restriction this IS 'sweet and soup on alternate days' — every day carries exactly one of the two, so no third rule is needed and none is added.
rules.name: corning_chakan_dessert_mon_wed_fri

rules._comment: 'Liquid sweets should not be considered' and (owner, 23 Nov) 'no kheer or payasam'. A ban, written as `max: 0` over the liquid desserts (the kheer / phirni / payasam / custard family). The flag alone let three payasams through — `dry_fruit_semiya_payasum`, `daliya_payasum` and `gulkand_firni` are filed `payasam_/_kheer` but not flagged liquid — so the whole kheer/payasam sub-category is named too.
rules.name: corning_chakan_no_liquid_sweets

rules._comment: 'All black dal preparations combined should be served maximum once a week.' Pune's three black dals (dal makhani, dhaba dal, maa ki dal) are one family for this purpose, which is what 'combined' means — a single rule over the flag, not one per dish.
rules.name: corning_chakan_black_dal_weekly

rules._comment: Rulebook Lunch/Dinner 3: 'Sprouts not to be served (gravy) for more than 02 days in a week.' A CEILING and nothing else. It carried `min: 2` as well, from an earlier instruction worded 'sprouts gravy at least twice a week', which FORCED two every week — the client has since confirmed the rulebook wording governs, so the floor is gone and a week with one or none is now compliant. Selected by name because Pune has no sprouts flag; the same selector is used by `corning_chakan_sprouts_not_with_potato`, deliberately, so two rules about sprouts cannot disagree about what a sprout is.
rules.name: corning_chakan_sprouts_gravy_twice_weekly

rules._comment: 'Paneer gravy should be included once a week across all meal sessions.' Exactly one day, so it is a floor as well as a cap — the client asked for the dish, not merely for a limit. Pune carries 18 paneer gravies.
rules.name: corning_chakan_paneer_gravy_weekly

rules._comment: 'Paneer/kofta preparations should be served once a week across lunch and dinner.' Read together with the rule above: the paneer gravy IS that once-a-week premium dish, and this caps the union so a kofta does not add a second such day. Stated as a cap only, because the floor is already carried by the paneer rule — two exact-1 rules over overlapping families would be a contradiction the moment the solver satisfied both with one dish.
rules.name: corning_chakan_paneer_or_kofta_weekly

rules._comment: 'Mixed-veg, veg kurma and veg kofta gravies should be served maximum twice a week.' The client stated a COMBINED number, so it gets its own rule over the union; Pune's ruleset separately caps each of the three at one day, which is stricter and stays in force. Written out because a future relaxation of a city rule must not silently relax the client's requirement too.
rules.name: corning_chakan_mixedveg_kurma_kofta_twice_weekly

rules._comment: 'Green leafy vegetable to be served once in a week' AND 'only two leafy-based dishes per week' — a floor and a ceiling, and until now only the ceiling was configured. Pune's own rule is `max_per_week: 1`; this overrides it by NAME so the two cannot disagree, raising the cap to 2 and adding the floor. The floor is the half that was missing and the half that was being broken: a real 7-day solve served ZERO leafy days and reported nothing, because every rule in play (this cap, Pune's cap, `leafy_daily_max_1`) is a ceiling and a week of none satisfies all three. R14's `leafy_veg_dry_15d_window` stays disabled above — once per 15 days cannot reach one a week, let alone two. SCOPE: veg_dry only, where Pune's rule put it; the client says 'leafy-based dishes', which may mean any slot, and widening it needs them to confirm.
rules.name: leafy_veg_dry_weekly

rules._comment: 'On Thursday only we will give a starter.' NEEDS A DB CHANGE FIRST: this counter has no `starter` category today, so until one is added the rule is inert and `diagnose()` says so. The restriction stands the station down on the other six days.
rules.name: corning_chakan_starter_thursday_only
corning_chakan_no_salad_on_the_chaat_day
rules._comment: Owner, 24 Nov: on the chaat day (the starter row, Thursday) salad and dressing are blank. Keep these days the complement of the starter rule's; tests/clients/test_corning_chakan_logic.py checks it.

rules.name: corning_chakan_no_dressing_on_the_chaat_day
rules._comment: Owner, 24 Nov: on the chaat day (the starter row, Thursday) salad and dressing are blank. Keep these days the complement of the starter rule's; tests/clients/test_corning_chakan_logic.py checks it.

'Starter should be chat item.' A one-slot composition component IS 'this slot must be a matching dish' (docs/repo_map.md note 20). Pune's starter pool holds four chaats (dhokla, kachori, papadi, samosa) against roughly four Thursdays inside the 20-day cooldown — it fits, with nothing spare, so a fifth chaat in the Pune list would give this rule some slack.
rules.name: corning_chakan_starter_is_a_chaat

rules._comment: 'Either flavour rice or white rice on a day, not both' — the flavoured-rice slot runs Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday. Same shape as Amadeus Pune (and Gartner, Ikea, Stryker NCR): two day-restrictions whose weekday lists are exact COMPLEMENTS, rather than a mutual exclusion between the two slots, so the pair can never both drop and leave a day with no rice at all. Before this both slots ran every day — a real 7-day solve served a flavoured rice AND steamed rice on all seven, which is what the client was reporting. Five flavoured days is the top of the stated 'four to five'. The days are fixed rather than solver-chosen because `white_rice` is a stamped constant, not a candidate the solver picks (src/constants.py CONST_SLOTS), so nothing in the model can trade one against the other. Standing the slot down on Wednesday costs no themed rice: this counter's theme_map makes Wednesday SOUTH, not biryani, and the biryani and khichdi cadences below still have five days to land on.
rules.name: corning_chakan_flavour_rice_mon_tue_thu_fri_sun

rules._comment: The other half: white rice on exactly the two days the flavoured-rice slot stands down. Written as its own weekday list rather than derived from the rule above because a constant slot is stamped AFTER the solve and has no cell to key off — a `slot_day_restriction` on a const slot used to be a silent no-op and the staple appeared every day anyway (menu_solver `_rows_to_week_plan` now honours skip_cells for them). The site serves seven days, so the two lists must union to all seven or a day comes out with no rice at all; if the flavoured-rice days change, this list changes with them.
rules.name: corning_chakan_white_rice_wed_sat

rules._comment: 'Biryani should be served maximum once in 15 days.' Pune's `mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly` caps the mixed-veg pulao/biryani family at one day a WEEK, which permits two inside any 15 days. This is the half that looks BACKWARDS, and it reads saved history rather than only the week being solved, so a plan starting the day after a biryani still waits. SELECTED BY NAME AS WELL AS FLAG, and the flag alone would have made this rule nearly inert: `is_biryani_item` is set on 3 of the 15 biryanis in Pune's rice pool, and a first version of this rule using the flag alone let a real week serve kolakata_stye_aloo_biryani on the Thursday and mughalai_veg_biryani on the Saturday while reporting zero. The missing flags are a dataset matter for the list's owner; the name carries the rule until they are set. `biryani_rice` is included deliberately — for a cap, counting an ambiguous dish costs a day of variety, missing one costs the rule. Paired with `corning_chakan_biryani_weekly` below, because this rule alone does not bind inside the week being solved: with it in place and no saved history, a real week served a biryani on the Thursday AND the Saturday. Pune uses the same pair for kadhi (`kadhi_weekly` + `kadhi_15d_window`) for exactly this reason.
rules.name: corning_chakan_biryani_15d_window

rules._comment: The forward half of 'biryani maximum once in 15 days': one biryani in the week being solved. The 15-day window above cannot see the week it is planning, only what was saved before it, so without this a single plan can hold two. Same selector as the window, deliberately — two halves of one requirement must not be able to disagree about what a biryani is. Pune's `mixedveg_pulao_biryani_weekly` stays in force and is stricter on the mixed-veg pulao family it names.
rules.name: corning_chakan_biryani_weekly

rules._comment: 'Khichdi once in fifteen days' is a CADENCE, so this rule is both halves. The ceiling is the 15-day backward window: no second khichdi inside fifteen days of a saved one. The floor is `at_least_once_per_window`: once the family has not been served for 15 days, the plan must serve one. The ceiling alone is satisfied by serving NONE — the sprouts-gravy defect of v2.07.01, a cap written where a floor was asked for, which reads as enforced and is not. Selected by sub_category, not by name: all seven khichdis in the Pune list are `north_khichdi` (dal_khichdi, masala_khichadi, moogdal_khichadi, moong_khichadi, palak_bajra_khichdi, khandeshi_khichadi, sweet_rice_pulao_khichadi) and the spelling runs khichdi / khichadi / khicha across them, so a name match would need three needles and would still miss the next one added. `is_liquid_rice` is set on one of the seven and is not the family. THE GUARANTEED GAP IS 15 DAYS PLUS THE HORIZON MINUS ONE (21 on a 7-day plan): the floor says 'somewhere in this plan', not 'on this date', because pinning the date would fix khichdi to one weekday for ever. The floor stands down, saying so, on a horizon where every khichdi is banned by the item cooldown. Lunch and dinner only: its floor would otherwise report itself relaxed on the breakfast and snacks menus, which have no rice row.
rules.name: corning_chakan_khichdi_15d_window

rules._comment: The forward half of 'khichdi once in fifteen days': at most one in the week being solved. Same selector as the window above, deliberately — two halves of one requirement must not be able to disagree about what a khichdi is.
rules.name: corning_chakan_khichdi_weekly

rules._comment: 'At least one of the dry/gravy vegetables should be a preparation of vegetables other than leafy vegetables & sprouts' — cauliflower, lady's finger, beans, cabbage, tondli, dodka, dudhi. A FLOOR across the two veg slots together, so `daily_min` on a two-slot `base_slot` list rather than a composition, which works on one slot. The excluded set also carries the non-vegetable preparations of the rule below: a besan or soya dish is neither leafy nor sprouts and would otherwise satisfy this floor while being exactly what the client does not count as a vegetable. `key_ingredient` is right for soy and besan but WRONG on three dishes that matter — `zunka` is filed `mixed_vegetables`, `sev_tamatar_bhaji` `tomato`, `simla_mirch_besan_ki_sabji` `chili` — which is the documented case for falling back to the name. `daily_min` relaxes per day and stamps the relaxation channel when a day's cells cannot place one.
rules.name: corning_chakan_a_real_vegetable_every_day

rules._comment: 'Do not serve 2 non-vegetable preparation in one meal' — pithla, sev bhaji, sandga curry, soya masala. A per-day CAP of one across the two veg slots. Pune carries almost none of the named examples (no pithla, no sandga) so the class is carried by `key_ingredient` soy (16 rows) and besan, plus the names for the three the column mis-files (see the rule above). `pithla`/`pitla`/`sandga` are listed although Pune has none today, so the rule covers them if the owner adds them. On this counter — exactly one veg_dry and one veg_gravy — this is implied by the floor above; both are kept because the client stated both and the implication breaks the moment a second veg slot is added.
rules.name: corning_chakan_one_non_vegetable_prep_per_meal

rules._comment: 'Eggplant (Brinjal/Wangi), sprouts (dry or gravy) and potato not to be served on one day.' Three families, read as no TWO of them sharing a day — the stricter reading, and the one the sentence supports. Two rules cover the three pairs: this one is brinjal against the other two, the next is sprouts against potato. `same_day_exclusion` is bidirectional and counts across every slot, which is the point — the client is talking about the day's plate, not one station. Brinjal must be matched by NAME: `key_ingredient == 'brinjal'` is set on ZERO Pune rows while three dishes are named for it (`bharali_wangi`, `bagare_baingan`, `aloo_baingan_masala`). NB `aloo_baingan_masala` is brinjal AND potato in one dish, so it matches both sides and the solver simply never places it — which is the client's intent, not a bug. Sprouts use the same selector as `corning_chakan_sprouts_gravy_twice_weekly` deliberately: two rules about sprouts must not disagree about what a sprout is.
rules.name: corning_chakan_brinjal_not_with_sprouts_or_potato

rules._comment: The third pair of 'eggplant, sprouts and potato not on one day': sprouts against potato. Separate from the rule above because `same_day_exclusion` bans one set against another and a single rule listing all three on both sides would ban each family against ITSELF. NOTE this is the pair that actually bites: `corning_chakan_sprouts_gravy_twice_weekly` FORCES two sprouts gravies a week, and potato is 75 of Pune's veg-slot rows, so two days a week are now closed to every aloo dish in every slot. A measured week served aloo_bhendi_amritsari beside sprouted_green_moong on the Monday, which is the violation this rule exists to stop.
rules.name: corning_chakan_sprouts_not_with_potato

rules._comment: Owner, 23 Nov ('Breakfast menu bank - Corning Chakan'): each breakfast combo is a main on the Breakfast Main row and its sides on the Accompaniments row (x3), exactly as the sheet pairs them; a blank cell where the combo has fewer sides. The sheet's plain 'chutney' is either breakfast chutney. A main is served at most once a week (unique_items), so no main repeats in a week.
rules.name: corning_chakan_breakfast_sides_follow_the_main

rules._comment: Owner, 23 Nov: each evening-snack combo is a snack on the Snack row and its sides on the Accompaniments row (x2); dabeli, panipuri, matki bhel and ragda pattice come with none.
rules.name: corning_chakan_snack_sides_follow_the_snack

rules._comment: Owner, 23 Nov ('Preffered items' sheet): the planner picks these first wherever the rules allow and fills the rest from the Pune list. A preference, not a limit (owner chose it): 27 dry vegs cannot fill 14 meals a week under the 20-day no-repeat. Names are the Pune list's (map reviewed with the owner, 23 Nov).
rules.name: corning_chakan_preferred_dishes

constant_items_by_meal._comment: 'Indian Bread staple only Chapati' — the same dish every day, which is what this fleet's rulebooks mean by a staple ('like white rice and pickle'). A pin, not a rule: a `slot_composition` or a `repeatable_items` on the chapati FAMILY would let the slot rotate between plain, palak, carrot and beetroot chapati, which is a variety rule where the client asked for one bread. Pinned to `chapati`, which is a real Pune row; `phulka` is the other dish Pune's R36 staple exemption names and it is not pinned, so the pin alone decides. Same shape as ICON Chn, DXC, SAEL and Corning NCR. Lunch and dinner only: a client-wide pin would also print at breakfast and snacks. Owner, 23 Nov ('Corning Menu option.xlsx'): salad and dressing fixed by weekday, the same at lunch and dinner. Thursday has none: it is the chaat day (owner). Dressing is its own row, not the chutney (owner: 'chutney and dressing are not the same').
